title: Chemistry — Mission 2: The Rusted Warning Sign
description: A corroded warning sign and a foaming spill in the same afternoon. Classify what's actually happening in each reaction before you write the incident report.

mika.name: Ms. Mika Tan
mika.description: Treats every incident report as a chance to test your reasoning.

dev.name: Dev
dev.description: Wants to write 'chemical stuff happened' and call it a day.

reaction_types_chart.name: Reaction Types Chart
reaction_types_chart.description: Synthesis, decomposition, single/double displacement, combustion — side by side.

ph_strip.name: pH Strip
ph_strip.description: Quick read on whether a spill is acidic, basic, or neutral.

elements.text: The outdoor sign rusted through over the weekend, and someone's spill in the hallway is still fizzing. Two reactions, two reports.
Can I just write 'a reaction occurred' for both?

elements.prompt: Mika hands you the reaction types chart.

options.text: "No — let's classify each reaction type first, that's what actually goes in the report."

elements.text: Good, chart in hand. Let's work through both scenes properly.
No chart yet — the report needs more than a shrug. Let's fix that.

config.question: The sign's iron reacted with oxygen and moisture to form iron oxide (rust): 4Fe + 3O2 -> 2Fe2O3. What type of reaction is this?

options.text: Synthesis (combination) — two or more substances combine into one
Decomposition — one substance breaks into multiple

config.explanation: Iron and oxygen combine into a single product, iron(III) oxide — a synthesis reaction.

config.prompt: The hallway spill was baking soda and vinegar: NaHCO3 + CH3COOH -> CH3COONa + H2O + CO2. What gas is causing the fizzing? (chemical formula)
Order these steps for writing up any reaction in an incident report, first to last.

items.text: Note any hazard (gas, heat, corrosive product)

elements.text: Synthesis for the sign, decomposition-driven gas release for the spill. That's a real report.
It's filed, but next time let's classify before we write anything down.

elements.prompt: The report is ready to submit. What now?

options.text: Show Dev how the reactant/product pattern predicts the reaction type every time.
File it and move on. Good enough for today.

elements.text: So you don't memorize which reaction is which — you just look at how many reactants go in and how many products come out. That's actually simple.

ending.title: Reaction Classifier
ending.description: Correctly classified both incidents from the equation pattern alone, and taught Dev the shortcut.

ending.title: Report Filed
ending.description: The incident report is submitted. The deeper classification lesson can wait.
